paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is an extremely uncommon arrhythmia that rarely appears familial. It has been associated with congenital heart disease, valvular heart disease, conduction disturbances, Brugada syndrome, myocardial infarction, and amyloidosis (Fazelifar et al., 2005). In affected individuals, P waves are absent on the surface ECG and the atrium cannot be captured by pacing (Makita et al., 2005).

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) and Makita et al. (2005) reported digenic inheritance of atrial standstill, involving a heterozygous SCN5A mutation together with polymorphisms in the GJA5 (Cx40) gene. In the family reported by Groenewegen et al. (2003), 5 unaffected relatives also carried the SCN5A mutation, and only the affected members had coinherited both the SCN5A mutation and the rare Cx40 genotype. In the family reported by Makita et al. (2005), the proband's father carried the SCN5A mutation but was in normal sinus rhythm. Makita et al. (2005) concluded that genetic defects in SCN5A most likely underlie atrial standstill, and that coinheritance of Cx40 polymorphisms is a possible genetic factor modifying the clinical manifestation, which may explain incomplete penetrance.

paragraphs.text: In a large family with atrial standstill, Groenewegen et al. (2003) carried out candidate gene screening and identified a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene (D1275N) in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives; the deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. Eight relatives were homozygous for 2 closely linked regulatory polymorphisms in the GJA5 (Cx40) gene (-44G-A and +71A-G), 3 of whom were affected. The 3 living patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A D1275N mutation. Homozygosity for both Cx40 polymorphisms was found in only about 7% of control subjects. In functional studies, D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels, and the rare Cx40 genotype caused reduced reporter gene expression compared with the more common Cx40 genotype. Groenewegen et al. (2003) proposed that, although the functional effect of each genetic change is relatively benign, their combined effect eventually progresses to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: In an 11-year-old boy with congenital atrial standstill, Makita et al. (2005) identified a heterozygous novel mutation in the SCN5A gene (L212P), inherited from his father, who was in normal sinus rhythm. Recombinant L212P channels showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of both activation (wildtype -48.1 mV vs L212P -63.5 mV) and inactivation (wildtype -86.6 mV vs L212P -95.6 mV), and delayed recovery from inactivation. Further screening for genetic variations that might mitigate L212P dysfunction showed that the proband, but not his father, carried Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
